record.title: Cube-cover conjecture for diagonalization games
record.statement:
Let $n$ and $m$ satisfy $2^{n-1}+1\leq m<2^n$, and set

$$
d=2^n-m<2^{n-1}.
$$

For a nonempty subset $J\subseteq[n]$, a **$J$-cube** is the set of binary vectors obtained by fixing all coordinates outside $J$ and allowing the coordinates in $J$ to vary. **Cube-cover conjecture.** For any collection $J_1,J_2,\ldots,J_q$ of nonempty subsets of $[n]$ satisfying

$$
\sum_{i=1}^q |J_i|=d,
$$

there are cubes $C_1,\ldots,C_q$ such that $C_i$ is a $J_i$-cube and

$$
\left|\bigcup_{i=1}^{q} C_i\right|\geq d+q.
$$

This condition is equivalent to Kronecker having a winning strategy when Cantor uses $mn-(2^n-m)$ queries. The statement concerns covering the Boolean cube under prescribed coordinate freedoms and would establish optimality of the proposed strategy; its resolution is not given in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, Olivier Bousquet, Kasper Green Larsen, Shay Moran and Shlomo Moran, “Diagonalization Games”, arXiv:2301.01924 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.01924

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2023).

record.title: The automorphism-group characterization for token graphs of connected Cartesian products
record.statement:
Let $G$) be a connected graph with $n\geq 5$ vertices and prime factor decomposition

$$
G=G_1\square\cdots\square G_r,
$$

where $r>1$. Let $\psi$ be the homomorphism from $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ to $\operatorname{Aut}(\mathbb{Z}_2^{[r-1]})$ defined by the induced permutation of the prime factors. **Automorphism-group characterization.** The automorphism group of the $k$-token graph of $G$ should satisfy

$$
\operatorname{Aut}(F_k(G))\simeq
\begin{cases}
\mathbb{Z}_2^{[r-1]}\rtimes_{\psi}\operatorname{Aut}(G) & \textrm{if } k=2,\\
\operatorname{Aut}(G)\times\mathbb{Z}_2 & \textrm{if } k=n/2,\\
\operatorname{Aut}(G) & \textrm{otherwise.}
\end{cases}
$$

This gives the complete automorphism group of the token graphs in the stated range, extending the preceding lower-bound result for $F_2(G)$. The parser supplies no evidence that the characterization has been proved or disproved, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Ruy Fabila-Monroy and Ana Laura Trujillo-Negrete, “On the Automorphism Group of Token Graphs of Complete Bipartite Graphs”, arXiv:2302.07914 (2025).

record.title: Extremal 3-product-free set conjecture for free semigroups
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be a finite set and let $\mathcal{F}$ be the free semigroup with alphabet $\mathcal{A}$. If $S\subset\mathcal{F}$ is 3-product-free and $d^{\ast}(S)=1/3$, consider the two types of label sets

$$
\{w\in\mathcal{F}:\text{the sum of the labels of letters in }w\text{ is }1\bmod 3\},
$$

and

$$
\{w\in\mathcal{F}:\text{the sum of the labels of letters in }w\text{ is }1,2\bmod 6\}.
$$

**Extremal 3-product-free set conjecture.** One of the following holds: either the letters of $\mathcal{A}$ can be labelled by $\mathbb{Z}/3\mathbb{Z}$ so that $S$ is contained in the first set, or the letters can be labelled by $\mathbb{Z}/6\mathbb{Z}$ so that $S$ is contained in the second set.

This is the free-semigroup analogue of the classification of extremal 3-sum-free sets in the non-negative integers. The density bound is established, but the extremal structure for $k=3$ is explicitly left open.
record.source_name: Freddie Illingworth, Lukas Michel and Alex Scott, “The structure and density of k-product-free sets in the free semigroup”, arXiv:2305.05304 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.05304

record.title: Aharoni–Ziv's matroidal Hall conjecture for finitary matroids
record.statement:
Let $M$ and $N$ be finitary matroids on the common ground set $E$. For $X\subseteq E$, write $M\!\upharpoonright\!X$ for the restriction of $M$ to $X$, and $N.X$ for the contraction of $N$ to $X$. A pair $(M,N)$ is matchable when $N$ has an $M$-independent base.

**Aharoni–Ziv's matroidal Hall conjecture.** There is no $M$-independent base of $N$ if and only if there exists an $X\subseteq E$ such that $M\!\upharpoonright\!X$ has an $N.X$-independent base, but $N.X$ has no $M\!\upharpoonright\!X$-independent base.

This conjecture generalizes Hall's theorem and Edmonds's finite matroid intersection criterion to finitary matroids on possibly infinite ground sets. The source notes that its formulation is equivalent to the slightly stronger “unhindered” condition used by Aharoni and Ziv; no resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Attila Joó, “Finite matchability under the matroidal Hall's condition”, arXiv:2305.12803 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.12803

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2023).

record.title: Lovett–Adiprasito–Kazhdan–Ziegler partition-rank conjecture
record.statement:
Let $V_1,\ldots,V_d$ be finite-dimensional vector spaces over a finite field $\mathbf{k}$, and let $f:V_1\times\cdots\times V_d\to\mathbf{k}$ be a multilinear form. Define the **partition rank** by

$$
\operatorname{prk}(f)=\min\left\{r:f=\sum_{i=1}^r g_i\cdot h_i\right\},
$$

where $g_i$ and $h_i$ are multilinear in disjoint sets of variables. Define the **analytic rank** by

$$
\operatorname{ark}(f)=-\log_q\frac{|Z|}{|V_1\times\cdots\times V_{d-1}|},
$$

where

$$
Z=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_{d-1})\in V_1\times\cdots\times V_{d-1}:f(x_1,\ldots,x_{d-1},\cdot)\equiv 0\}.
$$

**Lovett–Adiprasito–Kazhdan–Ziegler conjecture.** There exists a constant $C_d$ such that for any finite field and multilinear form $f$ we have

$$
\operatorname{prk}(f)\le C_d\cdot\operatorname{ark}(f).
$$

The inequality $\operatorname{ark}(f)\leq\operatorname{prk}(f)$ is known, and the conjecture asserts the reverse inequality up to a constant depending only on $d$.
record.source_name: Amichai Lampert, “Slice rank and analytic rank for trilinear forms”, arXiv:2404.19704 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.19704

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2024).

record.title: Conjecture on clique counts forcing long cycles in bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected bipartite graph with bipartition $(X,Y)$. Suppose

$$
|X|=n\le |Y|=b,
$$

let $h=\left\lfloor\frac{n-k}{2}\right\rfloor$, and assume that $\delta(G)\ge r\ge 1$, where $n\ge 2k+2r$ and $k\in\mathbb{Z}$. For positive integers $s$ and $t$, write $N(K_{s,t},G)$ for the number of copies of $K_{s,t}$ in $G$. **Clique-count long-cycle conjecture.** If

$$
N(K_{s,t},G)>\begin{cases}\max\{f_{s,t}(b,n,n-k,r),f_{s,s}(b,n,n-k,h)\},&s=t,\\[2pt]\max\{f_{s,t}(b,n,n-k,r)+f_{t,s}(b,n,n-k,r),\\f_{s,t}(b,n,n-k,h)+f_{t,s}(b,n,n-k,h)\},&s\ne t,\end{cases}
$$

then $G$ contains a cycle of length $2n-2k$. This conjecture proposes a clique-count extremal condition for forcing a cycle of the specified length in a not necessarily balanced bipartite graph; the supplied excerpt gives no resolution or further context for the functions $f_{s,t}$, so the claim remains open here.
record.source_name: Changchang Dong, Mei Lu, Jixiang Meng and Bo Ning, “The generalized Tur'an number of long cycles in graphs and bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2406.17371 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.17371

record.title: The $Q$-polynomial triple-intersection vanishing conjecture
record.statement:
Consider the $Q$-polynomial distance-regular graph $\Gamma=(X,\mathcal R)$, with standard module $V$, diameter $D$, and Krein parameters $q^h_{i,j}$. Let $\Lambda$ be the fundamental $\mathbb T$-submodule of $V^{\otimes 3}$, and let $E_h^{(1)},E_i^{(2)},E_j^{(3)}$ denote the corresponding tensor-factor operators. **The $Q$-polynomial triple-intersection vanishing conjecture.** For $0\leq h,i,j\leq D$,

$$
E_h^{(1)} E_i^{(2)} E_j^{(3)} \Lambda=0 \qquad\text{if and only if}\qquad q^h_{i,j}=0.
$$

This is the conjectural analogue for the ordinary primitive idempotents of the established statement involving the dual primitive idempotents and the intersection numbers $p^h_{i,j}$. It predicts that the vanishing pattern of these operator images on $\Lambda$ exactly records the vanishing of the Krein parameters.
record.source_name: Paul Terwilliger, “The S_3-symmetric tridiagonal algebra”, arXiv:2407.00551 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.00551

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

record.title: A theta-block crank conjecture for $(k+j)$-colored partitions
record.statement:
Let $k,j$ be positive odd integers. Let $q$ and $\tau$ be the variables in the generating function, let $\textbf{z}$ denote the crank variables, and let $\zeta$ denote the corresponding root-of-unity parameter. Choose $a_i$ to be consecutive even integers and $b_i$ to be consecutive odd integers. Define

$$
C_{k,j}(\textbf{z},\tau):= \prod_{n=1}^\infty\frac{(1-q^n)(1+q^n)(1+\zeta^{\pm a_1}q^n)(1+\zeta^{\pm a_2}q^n)\cdot\ldots\cdot(1+\zeta^{\pm a_{\frac{j-1}{2}}}q^n)}{(1-\zeta^{\pm b_1}q^n)(1-\zeta^{\pm b_2})\cdot\ldots\cdot(1-\zeta^{\pm b_{\frac{k+1}{2}}}q^n)}.
$$

**The theta-block crank conjecture.** The function $C_{k,j}(\textbf{z},\tau)$ defines a crank for the desired $(k+j)$-colored partitions and explains most of the Ramanujan-like congruences satisfied by their partition numbers.
The author suggests that theta-block theory may establish this general crank construction, analogously to prior work on crank generating functions. The statement is not accompanied by a resolution, and the paper does not specify precisely which congruences are covered by “most.”
record.source_name: Samuel Wilson, “A proposed crank for (k+j)-colored partitions, with j colors having distinct parts”, arXiv:2407.07891 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2407.07891

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2024).

record.title: Composition conjecture for lasso contractions
record.statement:
Let $(\operatorname{\mathcal{L}},\eta)$ be a lasso on a category $\mathsf{C}$. For monomorphisms $f_1\colon X_1\hookrightarrow Y$ and $f_2\colon X_2\to Y_{/f}$ arranged as in the source diagrams, let $Y_{/f_1}$ and $(Y_{/f_1})_{/f_2}$ denote the successive contractions, with induced maps $\eta_{X_1}^{\#}$ and $\eta_{X_2}^{\#}$. **Composition conjecture for lasso contractions.** There is a subobject $f\colon X\hookrightarrow Y$ whose lasso contraction satisfies

$$
Y_{/f}=(Y_{/f_1})_{/f_2}
$$

and

$$
\eta_X^{\#}=\eta_{X_2}^{\#}\eta_{X_1}^{\#}.
$$

The claim would imply that lasso-contractions are closed under composition, a prerequisite for making the relevant category of objects and lasso-contractions functorial. The source explicitly says that this general composition question is unresolved, although it is straightforward for graph contractions.
record.source_name: Benjamin Merlin Bumpus, James Fairbanks and Will J. Turner, “Lassos: Pushing Tree Decompositions Forward Along Homomorphisms”, arXiv:2408.15184 (2025).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15184

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2024). “A further open problem, possibly a more challenging one, is to determine whether pushing decompositions along morphisms is a functorial operation.”

record.title: Quantum graph isomorphism–strategy correspondence conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G:X\to X$ and $H:A\to A$ be irreflexive quantum graphs. The quantum graph isomorphism game is

$$
\lambda_{G\simeq H}:X\otimes X^\mathrm{op}\to A\otimes A^\mathrm{op},
$$

with

$$
\lambda_{G\simeq H}:=\lambda_{G\to H}\star\lambda_{H\to G}^\dagger.
$$

A quantum graph isomorphism from $G$ to $H$ is the corresponding structure-preserving quantum map. **Quantum graph isomorphism–strategy correspondence conjecture.** There is a one-to-one correspondence between quantum graph isomorphisms from $G$ to $H$ and quantum tensor bistrategies realizing perfect bicorrelations, with respect to a cup state, for the quantum graph isomorphism game $\lambda_{G\simeq H}$. The theorem preceding this conjecture establishes bisynchronicity, constructs perfect bicorrelations from quantum graph isomorphisms using quantum bistrategies and a cup state, and obtains quantum graph isomorphisms from perfect quantum commuting bistrategies; the full tensor-strategy correspondence remains unproved.
record.source_name: Adina Goldberg, “Quantum games and synchronicity”, arXiv:2408.15444 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.15444

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).

record.title: Bergold–Fabila-Monroy–Roldán-Pensado–Schaefer conjecture on empty cycles in simple drawings
record.statement:
A **simple drawing** of $K_n$ is a drawing of the complete graph in the plane with no self-intersecting edges, no crossings between adjacent edges, and at most one crossing between any pair of nonadjacent edges. A **plane cycle** is a cycle whose edges do not cross, and it divides the plane into two sides. An **empty $k$-cycle** is a plane cycle of length $k$ such that one of its sides contains no vertices in its interior. Bergold, Fabila-Monroy, Roldán-Pensado, and Schaefer conjectured that

$$
\text{every simple drawing of }K_n\text{ contains an empty }k\text{-cycle for each }3\leq k\leq n.
$$

**Bergold–Fabila-Monroy–Roldán-Pensado–Schaefer conjecture.** Every simple drawing of $K_n$ contains an empty $k$-cycle for each $3 leq k leq n$. The supplied paper proves the case $k=4$, even through every vertex, while the full assertion remains open there; the statement is known for convex drawings.
record.source_name: Helena Bergold, Joachim Orthaber, Manfred Scheucher and Felix Schröder, “Holes in Convex and Simple Drawings”, arXiv:2409.01723 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.01723

record.title: The canonical-drawing characterization of product structure for regular polygon intersection graphs
record.statement:
Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $\alpha$ be a parameter, and consider the class of intersection graphs of $\alpha$-free homothetic regular $n$-gons. A canonical drawing is a drawing associated with such an intersection representation, and a drawing is **$k$-independent crossing** if no edge is crossed by more than $k$ independent edges.

**The canonical-drawing characterization.** The class of intersection graphs of $\alpha$-free homothetic regular $n$-gons admits product structure if and only if their canonical drawings are $k$-independent crossing for a global constant $k$, possibly depending on $n$.

This conjecture proposes that product structure is exactly captured by bounded independent crossing in the canonical drawings; the paper establishes bounded independent crossing in one parameter regime but leaves the converse characterization open.
record.source_name: Laura Merker, Lena Scherzer, Samuel Schneider and Torsten Ueckerdt, “Intersection Graphs with and without Product Structure”, arXiv:2409.01732 (2024).

record.title: Finite-difference moment identities for elementary symmetric partition images
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal P(n)$ be the set of partitions of $n$, let $\mathcal P[m,n]=\biguplus_{i=m}^n\mathcal P(i)$, and let $\operatorname{ImP}_k[m,n]=\biguplus_{i=m}^n\operatorname{ImP}_k(i)$. Let $m_j$ denote the $j$th moment statistic and let $\Delta$ denote the finite-difference operator. **Finite-difference moment conjecture.** For $n\ge0$ and $k\ge2$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\Delta^{k-1}m_4(\operatorname{ImP}_k[n,n+1])&=m_2(\mathcal P(n))+m_4(\mathcal P[n,n+1]),\\
\Delta^{k-1}m_6(\operatorname{ImP}_k(n))&=m_6(\mathcal P(n))+m_2(\mathcal P(n-2))-m_3(\mathcal P(n-2)),\\
\Delta^{k-1}m_6(\operatorname{ImP}_k[n,n+1])&=m_3(\mathcal P(n))+m_6(\mathcal P[n,n+1]),\\
\Delta^{k-1}m_9(\operatorname{ImP}_k[n,n+2])&=m_3(\mathcal P(n))+m_9(\mathcal P[n,n+2]),\\
\Delta^{k-1}m_{10}(\operatorname{ImP}_k[n,n+1])&=m_5(\mathcal P(n))+m_{10}(\mathcal P[n,n+1]),\\
\Delta^{k-1}m_p(\operatorname{ImP}_k(n))&=m_p(\mathcal P(n)),
\end{aligned}
$$

where the last equality holds for $p=1$ or $p$ prime. These identities are proposed as a direction for future work, and the paper gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Cristina Ballantine, George Beck, Mircea Merca and Bruce Sagan, “Elementary symmetric partitions”, arXiv:2409.11268 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.11268

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).

record.title: The subdivision packing-coloring conjecture for subcubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a subcubic graph, meaning that every vertex of $G$ has degree at most $3$, and let $S(G)$ be the graph obtained by subdividing every edge of $G$ exactly once. A $(1,2,3,4,5)$-packing coloring assigns one of five colors to the vertices so that vertices receiving color $i$ are pairwise at distance greater than $i$.

**Subdivision packing-coloring conjecture.** The graph $S(G)$ admits a $(1,2,3,4,5)$-packing coloring. Equivalently, every subdivision of a subcubic graph has packing chromatic number at most $5$.

This conjecture was posed by Brešar, Klavžar, Rall, and Wash following a question of Gastineau and Togni. The supplied source evidence establishes it for generalized prisms of a cycle, except for the Petersen graph; the general statement is therefore recorded as solved according to the supplied status.
record.source_name: Boštjan Brešar, Kirsti Kuenzel and Douglas F. Rall, “Claw-free cubic graphs are (1, 1, 2, 2)-colorable”, arXiv:2409.15455 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.15455

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of September 2024). “In it was proved that generalized prisms of a cycle (with the exception of the Petersen graph) admit a $(1,1,2,2)$-packing coloring, hence Conjecture holds for this kind of cubic graph.”

record.title: The realization conjecture for winding-number invariants of almost embeddings of $K_4$
record.statement:
Let $K_4$ be the complete graph on vertices $1,2,3,4$, and let $f:K_4\to\mathbb R^2$ be an almost embedding. For an oriented cycle $C$ and a vertex $v$, write $w_f(C,v)$ for the winding number of the image of $C$ about $f(v)$. For $j\in[4]$, set

$$
\begin{aligned}
w_f(C_1,1)&=w_f(234,1),\\
w_f(C_2,2)&=w_f(134,2),\\
w_f(C_3,3)&=w_f(124,3),\\
w_f(C_4,4)&=w_f(123,4).
\end{aligned}
$$

**Realization conjecture.** For any integers $n_1,n_2,n_3,n_4$ whose sum is odd, there exists an almost embedding $f:K_4\to\mathbb R^2$ such that

$$
w_f(234,1)=n_1,\quad w_f(134,2)=n_2,\quad w_f(124,3)=n_3,\quad w_f(123,4)=n_4.
$$

This asserts that the parity condition supplied by the theorem that the corresponding signed sum is odd is the only restriction on these four winding numbers. The supplied text gives examples and references, but does not state whether the realization claim has been proved; its status is therefore left open.
record.source_name: E. Alkin, A. Miroshnikov and A. Skopenkov, “Invariants of almost embeddings of graphs in the plane”, arXiv:2410.09860 (2026).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.09860

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2024).

record.title: Poset-type conjecture for quadratic multiplicities of key-polynomial generating series
record.statement:
Let $w$ be a permutation, let $k$ and $l$ be positive integers, and let $A_l(w)$ and $A_k(w)$ be the sets of bounded increasing sequences associated with $w$. For a multi-set $\eta$, write $m^{k,l}_{\eta}(w)$ for its multiplicity, and partially order the set of presentations $\alpha+\beta=\eta$ with $\alpha\in A_l(w)$ and $\beta\in A_k(w)$ as described in the paper.

**Poset-type conjecture.** The multiplicity $m^{k,l}_{\eta}(w)$ depends only on the poset type of the set of sums $\alpha+\beta=\eta$, with $\alpha\in A_l(w)$ and $\beta\in A_k(w)$. Moreover, when one poset can be embedded into another, the associated multiplicity either remains the same or increases.

This extends the results known for $r\leq2$ to all values of $r$ and predicts that the quadratic multiplicities are governed solely by the combinatorial type of their presentation posets. The conjecture is posed after checking additional cases; no resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Noah Cape and Shaul Zemel, “Generating Series of Key Polynomials and Bounded Ascending Sequences of Integers”, arXiv:2411.08465 (2024).

record.title: Existence of a nice embedded tree
record.statement:
Let $X$ be a noncompact, metrizable generalized continuum. An **infinite rooted tree** is an infinite tree with a distinguished root, and a **proper embedding** is a topological embedding whose inverse images of compact sets are compact. The induced map on end spaces is denoted $E(\tau):E(T)\to E(X)$. **Existence of a nice embedded tree conjecture.** There exists an infinite rooted tree $T$ and a proper topological embedding

$$
\tau:T\rightarrowtail X
$$

such that

$$
E(\tau):E(T)\to E(X)
$$

is a homeomorphism. Moreover, $T$ may be chosen either to contain no leaves or so that the root is the unique leaf. This would provide a tree model for the end space of every noncompact metrizable generalized continuum, with additional control over the tree's leaves; the source presents it as a future direction and gives no known resolution.
record.source_name: William G. Bass and Jack S. Calcut, “Ends and end cohomology”, arXiv:2412.01816 (2025).
record.references:

record.title: Cactus-to-toggle factorization conjecture for minuscule crystals
record.statement:
Let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a simple Lie algebra, let $\lambda$ be a minuscule dominant weight, and let $w_0^J$ be the corresponding Weyl group element. Write $C_{\mathfrak{g}}$ for the cactus group, $Tog(w_0^J)$ for the toggle group, and $RPP(w_0^J,n)$ for the reverse plane partitions associated with $w_0^J$. The crystal $B(n\lambda)$ is identified with $RPP(w_0^J,n)$. **Cactus-to-toggle factorization conjecture.** There is a surjective map

$$
C_{\mathfrak{g}}\to Tog(w_0^J)
$$

such that the action of the cactus group on the crystal

$$
B(n\lambda)\cong RPP(w_0^J,n)
$$

factors through this map. In type $D_m$, the action of the cactus group on the crystal $B(n\varpi_1)$ is generated by cactus elements corresponding to length $1$ and $2$ subdiagrams of the Dynkin diagram. This conjecture proposes a uniform relationship between cactus-group actions and toggle actions beyond type $A$, extending the known connection between Berenstein--Kirillov involutions and cactus groups in type $A$ and the toggle models for minuscule Demazure crystals in $ADE$ types. The status of the proposed factorization and the type $D_m$ generation statement is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Devin Brown, Balazs Elek and Iva Halacheva, “Cacti, Toggles, and Reverse Plane Partitions”, arXiv:2412.02614 (2024).

record.title: Kempe state-reducibility conjecture for small configurations
record.statement:
A **configuration** is a local planar-map configuration, and a configuration is **Kempe state-reducible** when every $3$-face coloring on a state graph of its reducer is state-extendible to a $4$-face coloring on some state graph of the original, either directly or after a succession of Kempe switches on colorings on state-graph surfaces.

**Kempe state-reducibility conjecture.** At least one of the following configurations is Kempe state-reducible: a single pentagon, a single hexagon, two adjacent pentagons, or three pairwise-adjacent pentagons.

State-reducibility provides an alternative to ordinary reducibility because it does not rely on Kempe switches; the conjecture proposes that adding Kempe switches may make the method applicable to smaller configurations. Its resolution is not given in the paper.
record.source_name: Scott Baldridge and Ben McCarty, “A new way to prove configuration reducibility using gauge theory”, arXiv:2412.18558 (2024).

record.title: Geodesic Norine conjecture for antipodal edge-colorings of the cube
record.statement:
Let $Q_n$ be the $n$-dimensional cube graph, with vertices identified with binary strings of length $n$. For a vertex $u$, write $\bar u$ for the vertex with complemented bitstring; vertices $u$ and $\bar u$ are **antipodal**. An **antipodal edge-coloring** of $Q_n$ is a red/blue edge-coloring in which every pair of antipodal edges has different colors. A geodesic path between antipodal vertices has length $n$.

**Geodesic Norine conjecture.** For $n\ge 2$, every antipodal edge-coloring of $Q_n$ contains antipodal vertices $u$ and $\bar u$ joined by a monochromatic geodesic path.

Norine's original conjecture only requires a monochromatic path, which may be longer than $n$ edges; this geodesic version is stated as a mildly stronger conjecture. The original conjecture is known for $n\le 6$, and the paper verifies it for $n=7$ using SAT solvers; the status of the geodesic strengthening itself is not established in the supplied context.
record.source_name: Keith Frankston and Danny Scheinerman, “Proving Norine's Conjecture holds for n=7 via SAT solvers”, arXiv:2408.02474 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2408.02474

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2024).
